/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 20-year-old college student is brought to his primary care physician by his parents over the New Years holiday because they are concerned about his behavior since right after high school graduation in May the spring before. Prior to this year, he was generally an outgoing and social young man, who now reportedly has been spending the majority of his time alone in his dorm room and room at home, where his mother and father have overheard him talking to other people when he has no guests. When asked if anything was bothering him at school, he reports that at night the voice of the school's mascot encourages him to save the school from the large oak grove that will soon takeover the student union building by setting the trees on fire for all to see. On exam, his appears to be otherwise healthy and his urine toxicology screen is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Schizoaffective disorder
B. Major depression
C. Schizophrenia
D. Schizophreniform disorder
E. Malingering

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns psychiatric symptoms and diagnosis of a psychotic disorder, which falls within the mental health scope of MedX."}
